scenes.title: The Party at Shepard's Apartment
scenes.when: 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the clone was stopped and the Normandy retaken, before Cronos Station
scenes.where: Shepard's personal apartment on the Wards — two floors, kitchen, bar by the window, poker den, balcony, hot tub, rock garden

beats.text: Joker suggests the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy. Shepard buys Party Provisions from the kiosk at the bar on the second floor of the Silver Coast Casino for 100 credits, then sends the invitations from the private terminal in the apartment office.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez and Samantha Traynor are automatic. Everyone else is an optional invite, and only surviving squadmates whose Mass Effect 3 arcs are finished can come at all.

Absences nobody explains: Gardner, Allers, Chakwas, Chambers, Adams, Donnelly and Daniels are all missing. Traynor mentions in the kitchen that Chakwas is dealing with a medical emergency on the Citadel. The rest are simply not addressed.
Glyph asks the Commander what kind of party this is — quiet or energetic — and the answer sets the opening conversations. The groupings themselves are set by the guest list, not the theme.

Opening arrangement: Liara and Traynor in the kitchen with Tali, Samara and Garrus. EDI and Joker at the bar by the window with Miranda and Jacob. James and Cortez on the couches by the piano with the Virmire survivor and Jack. Wrex and Grunt upstairs on the balcony with Zaeed and Javik. Kasumi flits between the bar and the kitchen, uncloaking to interject.

Wrex and Grunt spend the opening trading krogan insults over who is stronger — Grunt calling Wrex a fossil and belittling his age. If the mood is energetic they headbutt each other to settle it and Shepard has to stop them before the furniture goes.
Grunt tells Wrex that two of Aralakh Company's recruits had opposed his appointment, and that only one of them had to be dealt with, the other having been killed in a fight.

Garrus's verdict on the place is that it would be a good place to retire, its sightlines appealing to his sniper sensibilities. He complains at a quiet party about the lack of hard drinks and at an energetic one dares Shepard to try the swill on offer.

Traynor cannot get over the size of the apartment — the electric bill alone would have covered her college tuition. Tali's version is that the same bill would have bought her an air conditioner for her suit, which she does not have, and it gets hot in there.
The group toasts the Normandy. Traynor admits she still feels like an outsider next to people who have histories with Shepard, and everyone weighs in.

Traynor gets everyone recounting how they met Shepard. Tali's memory is that all she could think about was hoping Shepard had showered, because her filter needed replacing and humans carry a lot of germs. Liara notes that three years on she is drinking Shepard's booze through a straw, and calls that progress.

Second phase, energetic: Liara and James argue on the balcony about whether biotics or muscle wins, with Jacob, Miranda, Jack, Kaidan and the Virmire survivor taking sides. James shows off his "fine example of peak physical form"; Liara says she is going to challenge him to a pull-up contest, which gives him pause. When James jabs at "flawed implants," Kaidan shoots back with how hard he has worked and his resulting ability to Reave, drawing trepidation from Liara and Jacob. Shepard picks a side. If Shepard backs biotics, Liara lifts him off the floor with no visible effort and Kasumi uncloaks to goad him into sit-ups; if Shepard backs muscle, the push-ups happen instead and Kaidan is flabbergasted, though Shepard can comfort him by saying that his kind of physical excellence is Shepard's kind too.

Second phase, energetic, at the bar: Joker gets ganged up on by Cortez, Garrus, Wrex and Javik or Zaeed over refusing to keep a sidearm in the cockpit. Garrus's line is that a weapon he cannot get to is no weapon at all. Wrex offers Tuchanka as the harshest planet alive and dares anyone present to last a day there, says krogan parties involve a lot of violent deaths, and announces he needs to shoot something. If Shepard keeps the mood up and backs the shooting practice, he makes good on it — bottles on the counter, with Javik and Zaeed joining in.

Second phase, energetic, at the door: Grunt works the vid-phone as bouncer, distinguishing fake salarian lip-hair from the real thing and establishing that Shepard has no half-brother named Sheppy the Volus. He is briefly tempted by cookies and turns them away anyway.

Second phase, quiet: Grunt dares Wrex into a drinking contest and will not accept his excuses, goading him with "logic is for salarians" and the observation that the great Urdnot Wrex has backed down from a challenge. Elsewhere Liara and James compare the SSV Normandy with the SR-2 in the den, with Tali acting out both ships' handling and engine noise and reporting that the SR-2 is harder to perform. Garrus and Zaeed stand on the balcony discussing how to make the apartment defensible. Kaidan, Joker and Samantha discuss EDI on the second floor.
Traynor and Joker — or Traynor and EDI, extremely awkwardly — work through Traynor's recorded opinion of EDI's voice, while Tali nearly poisons herself with cheese trying to change the subject.

Third phase, quiet: Tali ends up on the floor of the downstairs bathroom, wasted and barely comprehensible, having got an omni-tattoo at Jack's suggestion. Shepard tells her to get some rest and hears fragments of her muttering while passing the door afterwards. Grunt is wherever the food or the drink is, announcing his hunger. Liara and James play cards in the den with Javik and a cloaked Kasumi, Glyph dealing if Shepard sends it there.

Third phase, energetic: Grunt is wasted under the running shower upstairs, muttering about being a Space Cowboy, asking whether someone is a wizard, mourning that hanar cannot wear sweaters and reporting that he found a blue rock for Liara. Downstairs the dancing starts between the kitchen and the conference room — Traynor, Cortez, Jack, Samara, Garrus and Tali — with Glyph setting up the floor if sent. Kasumi is in the downstairs bedroom closet going through Shepard's underwear drawer.

Garrus on watching Shepard dance: record it and broadcast it at the Reapers, because they will either run, melt down, or fall in love. Someone starts reciting the periodic table; at "element 69" the humans snicker and Garrus reminds them it is thulium.

Garrus's quiet-party alternative is micro-filaments — tiny explosives laid in a grid across the glass by the door that shred anyone coming through — coordinated with Zaeed over comms, and he later gets to name a booby-trapped coffee maker "caffeine rush".

At the end Shepard assembles everyone by the couch for a group photo. Couples face each other; everyone else looks at the camera. The photograph hangs afterwards by the downstairs bar, opposite the fireplace.

variants.text: Miranda and Jack end up in the den insulting each other. Shepard can push them to reconcile or egg them on; Kasumi uncloaks either way and makes it worse.
Liara calls the apartment the "Shepard-Vakarian love nest"; if Shepard is with someone else, Garrus is the one making the love-nest joke and promising not to interrupt.

Ashley sits with James by the ground-floor couches in the first phase, teasing Cortez. In an energetic second phase, if she and James are both unromanced, James tries to recruit her to his side of the biotics-versus-muscle argument; she flirts back and takes an interest in his physique, and if Shepard encourages the two of them the night pushes them closer without anything coming of it — James tries out a line of Spanish on her that only leaves her asking him to repeat himself. If either of them had been turned down by Shepard first, Ashley alternates between attraction and rejection instead and declines to back James in the argument. During a relaxed third phase, if Wrex is present he recounts being ready to kill for the genophage cure back on Virmire and asks Ashley whether she would have shot him; she says without hesitation that she would have if he'd left her no choice, and Wrex says he respects her for it.

beats.text: Garrus denies having judged the quarians the way Tali says he did, then stops and apologises properly, admitting he was wrong about them.

Tali's read is that losing Palaven gave him a new perspective on her people, and he agrees. He turns her own opening question back on her — any regrets about serving on a human ship — and she has none.

Elsewhere Tali asks EDI why the Reapers have not made husks of quarians. EDI's answer is not that they are useless but that the Reapers have not met them in numbers, and that the Normandy has benefited enormously from quarian engineering. Tali takes the comfort and thanks her.

Glyph accompanies Liara throughout Shepard's identity theft fiasco. It purchases tickets and make reservations to a fundraiser on the Silver Coast Casino that has a lead on Shepard's situation, and later reports activity at the Citadel Archives. As Shepard brings the entire team out on a mission, Glyph follows into the archives as well. It gets repeatedly confused by Shepard's clone, as well as sidetracked by various historical information held in the archives, such as information on elcor mating rituals. During fights, Liara instructs Glyph to lower the enemy's morale. It hovers over various targets and tells them statistical data on the likelihood of their survival, as well as various benefits that come with joining the Alliance military. Glyph later helps free Shepard and the squad when they are trapped and abandoned in iridium vaults by the clone and Maya Brooks. Glyph helps Shepard organize a party in the aftermath of the clone incident. When the party gets going at the Personal Apartment, Glyph adds a bow\-tie to its holographic avatar, and asks Shepard what mood to set for the party. If Shepard set the ambience for a quiet party, Glyph can either help with food or drink preparation. It accompanies Samantha Traynor in either case. If a loud party is chosen instead, Glyph can either observe the guests dancing at the balcony or the people playing poker downstairs. Whichever way the party ends, it is used to take a photograph of the gang.

The Personal Apartment was a location on the Citadel, in Tiberius Towers on the Silversun Strip, introduced in the Citadel DLC for Mass Effect 3. It originally belonged to Admiral David Anderson, who planned to retire there with Kahlee Sanders. While the Normandy SR-2 was docked at the Citadel for repairs, Anderson gave the apartment to Commander Shepard as a place to relax during shore leave. It included a weapon bench, armor locker, private terminal, and a furnishings catalog for items bought from Home Spun on the Strip. Scattered through the apartment were audio recordings of parts of Anderson's biography, including an unfinished interview with reporter Khalisah al-Jilani.

The apartment had two floors: a ground floor with a large seating area, fireplace, bar, piano, kitchen with a Normandy SR-2 model, a bedroom, and a smaller living room holding the Private Terminal and Catalog; and a first floor with an art gallery, a second seating area, Shepard's large bedroom with the armor locker and weapon bench, an en-suite bathroom with a hot tub, and a third bedroom. Squadmates and other characters could be summoned to the apartment or invited out onto the Strip after messages arrived at the private terminal; some characters had one interaction on the Strip and a second in the apartment, in fixed order.

Accessories accumulated through play: a plush volus doll and stereo music tracks won from the Claw Game at Castle Arcade, a trophy left by Samantha Traynor after a visit, a photo of Thane Krios left on the piano after Kolyat's visit, and Glyph playing Liara's song on the piano. The Anderson biography recordings covered his London childhood (born June 8, 2137), his enlistment, service in the First Contact War, N7 training, his first meeting with a salarian Spectre, cross-species training on Palaven under Bartus Aurix, his failed marriage, the design of the Normandy SR-1, and his decision to release the Normandy to Shepard before the Battle of the Citadel. Associated missions included Citadel: Shore Leave, Citadel: Identity Theft, and Citadel: Party.

The Silversun Strip was a hub location on the Citadel Wards introduced in Mass Effect 3's Citadel downloadable content. It contained the Armax Arsenal Arena, Shepard's Personal Apartment, the Silver Coast Casino, Castle Arcade, a bar, and a Rapid Transit point, and served as a second social hub where Shepard could meet current and former squad members after receiving e-mail invitations. These encounters depended on the ally's own mission being complete, and some allies had a first meeting on the Strip and a later one in the Apartment.

Points of interest included the Personal Apartment (with the Home Spun kiosk and, for a Spacer Shepard, the ability to call Hannah Shepard), the Armax Arsenal Arena (with a vorcha Three-card Monte hustler outside and procurement and weapon-upgrade terminals), Castle Arcade (featuring Shattered Eezo, the Claw Game, Relay Defense, and a powered-down Towers of Hanoi), the Silver Coast Casino (Quasar, roulette, varren racing, and Kasumi Goto's suspicious device), and the bar where Citadel: Party supplies were sold and Garrus Vakarian, Ashley Williams, Joker, and Urdnot Wrex could be met.

Missions staged here included Citadel: Shore Leave, Citadel: Identity Theft I and II, Silver Coast Casino: Infiltration, Citadel: Party, and numerous Armax Arsenal Arena challenges. Notable background NPCs included Francis Kitt promoting a krogan-led production of Macbeth and an out-of-work elcor actor who quoted Hamlet. Arena and arcade high-score boards listed characters such as Aria T'Loak, Barla Von, Khalisah al-Jilani, Bray, Matriarch Aethyta, Schells, Armando-Owen Bailey, Mouse, and James Vega. Several overheard conversations referenced Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode.

Citadel: Party was a Mass Effect 3 mission in the Citadel DLC in which Commander Shepard hosted a gathering at the Personal Apartment during shore leave. Joker suggested the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy SR-2 in Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy. To prepare, Shepard bought Party Provisions for 100 credits, or 90 with both Intel Terminal discounts, from a kiosk at the Silver Coast Casino bar, then sent invitations from the apartment's private terminal. The party had to be held before Priority: Cerberus Headquarters, after which the DLC content closed.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez, and Samantha Traynor were auto-invited as guaranteed survivors. All other guests were optional and required surviving all three games with their Mass Effect 3 arcs complete: Garrus, Grunt, Jacob, Jack, Javik, Kasumi, Samara, Zaeed, Wrex, Ashley or Kaidan, Tali, and Miranda Lawson, each with specific prerequisites. Squadmates fated to die in their arcs, Legion and Thane Krios, did not appear; Mordin Solus would not break cover even if he survived; Morinth was absent. Other Normandy crew such as Karin Chakwas could not attend, with Traynor stating Chakwas was handling a medical emergency on the Citadel.

Glyph asked Shepard to pick a Quiet or Energetic theme, which set dialogue but not group arrangements. The party ran in phases: an opening, a second part where Shepard could keep or switch the theme and settle guest disagreements, and a final phase whose arrangements followed the second theme, with Shepard choosing which group Glyph joined. Kasumi repeatedly uncloaked to interject. Conversations covered the two Normandys, biotics versus muscle, Joker's refusal to keep a gun in the cockpit, and Miranda and Jack's feuding. The phase ended with a Group Photo, later hung near the downstairs bar, in which romantic couples faced each other.

Shepard woke in the aftermath, potentially beside a love interest; an unromanced female Shepard could wake with James Vega or Javik. If Mordin had survived through the genophage arc, a datapad of his recordings lay by the bed. The guests dispersed around the apartment before Shepard signaled Rapid Transit to return everyone to Docking Bay D24. The Normandy crew gathered at the observation window; if Shepard had romanced Thane, his spirit appeared to speak to his siha before Shepard boarded last, closing the DLC. The Silversun Strip remained accessible afterward. Mark Meer later said Shepard's final franchise line, recorded for this mission, was "The best."

Citadel: Shore Leave was the Mass Effect 3 mission that opened the main storyline of the Citadel DLC, available after Priority: The Citadel II. Shepard activated it by reading a private terminal message from Admiral Hackett ordering the Normandy into dry dock on the Citadel for retrofits and putting the crew on shore leave, with a note that Admiral Anderson kept an apartment on the Wards.

Traveling to the Personal Apartment, Shepard was contacted by Anderson from Earth, who handed the apartment over permanently, saying he no longer needed it. After exploring, Shepard read a message at the private terminal from Joker proposing dinner at the Ryuusei sushi restaurant in the Wards. At the restaurant, the host let Shepard bypass the queue. Joker discussed the Normandy's dry docking, and Shepard could remind him it was shore leave or agree with his distrust of the engineers for morality points. Joker then asked why Shepard had invited him, and Shepard replied that Joker had sent the invitation, leaving both confused.

An Alliance soldier in dress uniform who had been trying to get Shepard's attention reached the table and introduced herself as Staff Analyst Maya Brooks of Alliance intelligence. She warned that a new group was trying to kill Shepard, hacking Shepard's account and communications and targeting the Spectre personally. Shepard told her to calm down and start from the beginning, which began the next mission, Citadel Wards: Ambush. As in the main game, Ashley or Kaidan, Javik, and Tali were only available as squadmates for the DLC if they had been recruited. Preparations such as purchases and power selection could not be made once Shepard docked at the Personal Apartment, and the following mission imposed a weight capacity penalty.

Garrus Apologises to Tali. 2186, after Rannoch aboard the Normandy SR-2 Garrus denies having judged the quarians the way Tali says he did, then stops and apologises properly, admitting he was wrong about them.

Garrus Apologises to Tali. 2186, after Rannoch aboard the Normandy SR-2 Elsewhere Tali asks EDI why the Reapers have not made husks of quarians. EDI's answer is not that they are useless but that the Reapers have not met them in numbers, and that the Normandy has benefited enormously from quarian engineering. Tali takes the comfort and thanks her.

Garrus Apologises to Tali. 2186, after Rannoch aboard the Normandy SR-2 Tali's read is that losing Palaven gave him a new perspective on her people, and he agrees. He turns her own opening question back on her — any regrets about serving on a human ship — and she has none.

Following the destruction of the Reaper on Rannoch, the geth are weakened and Admiral Han'Gerrel launches a full strike. The geth unit Shepard and Tali rescued from the geth dreadnought, either Legion itself, or a Geth VI constructed in its likeness, attempts to upload the Reaper code to augment all intelligences of the geth collective: an act that would restore the geth to full strength, catching the quarian fleet unaware and leading to their destruction. If Shepard allows the geth to be upgraded, Tali watches in horror as she witnesses the entirety of the Migrant Fleet crash and burn up in Rannoch's atmosphere. Filled with despair, she removes her mask, whispers "I'm sorry", and commits suicide by throwing herself off a cliff. Shepard tries desperately to catch her but to no avail. If Shepard stops the geth unit from uploading the code, it becomes hostile and Tali is forced to stab it with her boot knife to save Shepard. If Legion is alive and Shepard convinces the quarians to halt their attack, peace is achieved between the quarians and the geth, and Tali watches sadly as Legion sacrifices itself to grant autonomy to all geth, but not before confirming that the answer to Legion's question—whether or not the geth have souls—was 'Yes'. If Shepard chose to side with the quarians over the geth, instead of seeing hope the victory reminds Tali of the losses she incurred: her team on Haestrom, her father, and even Legion if the platform was around. She starts thinking she isn't ready to settle down yet. In all cases where she survives the aftermath, Tali decides to rejoin the Normandy, knowing that she'd be fighting for her homeworld. Before leaving Rannoch, she takes off her mask to see the sunset. While on the Citadel, Tali coordinates her people's activities with the turians. Shepard can find her on the Presidium Commons conversing with a functionary, either a diplomat or a clerk depending on the time. Before the battle for Rannoch, Tali argues with a diplomat for medical supplies, but the turian insists that they have nothing to spare. Tali points out the quarians are willing to pay and that thousands will die without the meds, but the turian counters that with the ongoing war and the recent failed coup the turians themselves don't have much supplies to go around. Shepard can step in and reason with either party, but the end result is the same: no meds for the quarians. Tali is grateful for the token support if Shepard sides with her, or grudgingly concedes the turian's point and tells the Commander she'll talk later if otherwise. If she survived the battle for Rannoch, Tali becomes the quarians' ambassador on the Citadel. Shepard finds her conversing with a clerk, whom Tali identifies as the one who denied her asylum when she acquired evidence of Saren's treachery. The turian doesn't recognize her and Tali decides not to remind him, realizing that war is no time for petty grudges. During the aftermission lulls, Tali often banters with Garrus, EDI and Chief Engineer Adams. She and Garrus have several conversations regarding their earlier missions with Shepard. While discussing those missions, Garrus claims the one on Horizon was the toughest. Tali complains as she hasn't joined up at the time; if Garrus wasn't on Shepard's team yet during Liara's rescue on Therum, Tali recalls the particularly difficult fight with the krogan battlemaster in the Prothean ruins. Next, she asks about the creepiest thing they fought, and Tali opines it was the rachni, particularly the small spider\-like swarmers. Garrus jabs that she supposedly likes things up close and personal, though Tali makes an exception for spiders. In a subsequent conversation, Tali asks Garrus if he has any regrets about serving on a human ship. Garrus reminds her that the original Normandy was co\-developed by turians. When pressed, he teases her that he had to serve on the Normandy to prevent her from making "dextros" look bad. Continuing with the repartee, Tali pointedly brings up past comments Garrus had made that were critical of her species. Garrus initially denies this, but eventually apologizes sincerely, admitting he was wrong to judge the quarians the way he did. Tali suggests that losing Palaven to the Reapers gave him a new perspective on her people, to which he agrees. Garrus then turns Tali's initial question about having any regrets about serving on a human ship back on her; she responds that she has none. Tali also talks with EDI regarding Reaper conversion of the different races into husks, deliberating on why they haven't started converting the quarians. EDI assures her that it is not that Reapers don't consider them useful, rather that they have not encountered Tali's race in large numbers.

If Shepard chooses to activate the Crucible, Garrus will be the last person Shepard sees before ending the Reaper threat. If Shepard chooses to control the Reapers or merge organic and synthetic life, Garrus will be seen placing Shepard's name on the memorial wall, or, if Shepard chooses to destroy the Reapers and enough of the galaxy's forces have been mustered, he will smile and refrain from placing the plaque, and the Normandy is seen flying off. If Shepard chose to merge organic and synthetic life, Garrus will place the Commander's name on the memorial wall. After that, he will share a hug with EDI. If neither Garrus nor Tali'Zorah vas Normandy developed relationships with Shepard back during the campaign against the Collectors, they enter a romantic relationship with each other and Shepard may walk in on them embracing each other in the Main Battery. Caught in the act, they both make a hasty excuse that one of Garrus's mandibles may have gotten hooked on Tali's helmet, and that Tali asked for him to check for a rupture. Shepard is happy for the two of them, and the two thank the Commander. Garrus supposes it helps knowing that there is something to go back to, though Tali claims the relationship is a fling and she is "using \[him] for \[his] body." Garrus quips that she's mean but he's okay with it. Bits of their intercom conversations indicate they were headed in that direction. While comparing toughest missions and creepiest enemies, Garrus particularly notices when Tali jabs him about keeping "everything at a distance." He asks her about it, though Tali insists she doesn't mean anything. When Tali shares her aversion to spiders, Garrus teases that she was supposed to like things up close and personal; she clarifies that "it depends on who it is."

evidence.text: If Shepard romances neither Garrus nor Tali, then near the end of Mass Effect 3 the two of them can be caught together, flustered and improvising excuses ("I think one of my mandibles got hooked on her helmet… infection risks…"). Tali plays it down — "This is just a fling, Vakarian. I'm using you for your body." — "You're so mean." — "And I'm okay with that." Garrus notes it helps to have something to come back to.

Shepard counters that at every decision some die while others live. Whatever Shepard's opinion, Garrus begins to realize the Commander's point and the necessity for leaders who don't give a damn about consequences. If the ruthless calculus of war dictates that ten billion die so that twenty billion can live, Garrus asks if they are prepared for such sacrifice. If Tali'Zorah vas Normandy is around, Garrus occasionally talks to her via intercom. At one time they compare notes about their personal toughest missions and creepiest enemies. Garrus goes with the mission to Horizon as his toughest, though Tali takes umbrage since she wasn't with the team yet, so Garrus claims the one aboard the derelict Reaper instead. Tali realizes it's because the close quarters nature of that mission conflicts with Garrus' sniper nature, and he agrees. As for the creepiest thing they fought, Garrus either recalls the Thorian or the bugs in the Collector swarm. Garrus is puzzled when Tali claims the rachni, either because they didn't fight the Rachni Queen both times or clarifying if she was talking about the original queen or the Breeder. Tali explains it's about the small spider\-like swarmers, prompting Garrus to tease that she was supposed to like things up close and personal, though she makes an exception for the spiders. In a subsequent conversation, the two discuss whether they harbor any regrets about choosing to serve aboard a human ship. Garrus reminds Tali that the original Normandy was co\-developed by turians; he also teases her that he had to serve on the Normandy to prevent her from making "dextros" look bad. When Tali pointedly brings up past comments he had made that were critical of her species, Garrus apologizes sincerely for his past prejudices, claiming youthful ignorance. He agrees with her observation that losing his own homeworld may have given him greater perspective on the quarians. Following the rescue mission of Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib\-Qwib, Garrus establishes a connection to his father still stranded on Palaven, trying to get to the escape shuttles. Garrus's sister, Solana, broke her leg but the injury isn't life\-threatening. However, the connection dies before Garrus could talk more. He silently mutters a prayer to the turian spirits, wishing to see his family again. After the mission on Thessia, Garrus learns that his family has successfully fled from Palaven. It is immediately followed by bad news, however, as Garrus has just advised Primarch Victus to issue a full retreat against the Reapers and to hold back their ships until the Crucible's completion. He has now gambled everything on the Crucible and "ruthless calculus." If Shepard went through with curing the genophage, Garrus shifts his concerns toward Shepard's well\-being. Whether Shepard admits to weariness of the war or stubborn rejection of fatigue, Garrus attempts to cheer the Commander up in his capacity as a friend regardless of response. If Shepard decided to sabotage the cure on Tuchanka, Garrus takes notice on how the salarians had chosen to commit resources to the war despite the genophage "cure" and wonders how the Commander had managed that, additionally asking if Wrex jumping Shepard at the Citadel had anything to do with it (if that happened). At this point Shepard can either come clean or avoid the questioning. If the Commander decides to come clean with this, Garrus assures Shepard that he would have done the same to save Palaven under the same desperate circumstances. Garrus inquires whether the salarian scientist willingly went along with Shepard's plan. If the scientist did not, Shepard doesn't reply, to which Garrus swears at the war. If they did, however, Garrus is astounded. If Mordin was the scientist, Garrus calls him a devious salarian before realizing the implication. With Wiks, Garrus just jumps to the implication of tricking Wreav. If Wrex was once a member of Shepard's team before dying on Virmire, Garrus remarks that the krogan might've figured it out but his replacement brother Wreav is just too stupid. Otherwise, he states that Wreav scares him. In any case, Garrus opines that he can't tell the Urdnot leader what he thinks. Garrus compliments Shepard for playing both sides and asks that he be reminded to never play poker with Shepard. If Shepard still kept the truth from Garrus, either by mentioning "a disagreement about strategy" with Wrex or "careful negotiation about strategy" with the salarians otherwise, Garrus states that he won't be one to judge if that "strategy" involved paying a price to save Earth. Garrus has a few more things to say after the topic on ruthless calculus. He tries to point out Thessia's fall wasn't the Commander's fault: the world was already gone by the time they arrived.

Sometimes Tali will say something spontaneously, without being prompted. - During Priority: Eden Prime: - Near the beginning of the mission, Tali jokingly asks Liara if she ever found a dinosaur. When Liara realizes that Tali was joking, she remarks "Maybe a little." - After finding the dead colonists, Tali will say that the Fleet would make examples of pirates and slavers that attacked the civilian ships. - During Attican Traverse: Krogan Team: - If Grunt is alive, Tali will note that he is a good choice for the mission \- not that she doesn't expect to find sophisticated equipment in a cave filled with poisonous gas and monsters. - If Grunt died or was never let out of his tank, if the other squadmate's spot isn't filled by EDI, Garrus or Kaidan, Tali simply comments that maybe they can find out what happened to the scouts. - On the container with the weapon bench, if you wander close to the edge of the open space Tali comments it's a long way down. - If James is not the other squadmate Tali will scream "spiders, spiders, spiders, **spiders!**" when Swarmers are released from the first group of gestation pods. - During Tuchanka: Bomb: - If Garrus is not the other squad member Tali will remark that planting a bomb on the krogan homeworld is unforgivable since the turians have already won. - If Garrus is the other squad member Tali will respond to one of Garrus's comments about the bomb by saying it was "monstrous." - During Priority: Geth Dreadnought: - When Tali presents Shepard with the Arc Pistol and Garrus is the other squadmate and asks why he doesn't get a new gun, Tali will tell Garrus that she couldn't find one for his size. - Upon entering the geth defense network, if Tali was chosen as the Specialist Technician on the suicide mission in Mass Effect 2, she and Shepard will comment about the experience and how she "got set on fire." - During Rannoch: Admiral Koris: - Just after debarking the shuttle at the start of the mission, Tali will express her amazement at standing in the land of her ancestors centuries after her people's exile. - Early on, if Liara is the other squadmate, she notes the large numbers of geth present. Tali responds that they are "cleanup crews" as the geth never learned to capture their enemies alive. - Early on, if Garrus is the other squadmate, he muses that asteroids could be towed in to win the war against the geth. Tali is aghast, as such a tactic would render Rannoch uninhabitable. Garrus argues lamely that the dust clouds would settle after a few centuries. - During Kallini: Ardat\-Yakshi Monastery: - When wandering in the dark at the beginning of the mission Tali will claim that she tripped only if the other squadmate is either James, Javik or EDI. - After the battle with the first Banshee, Tali will remark, "That used to be an asari?" If Liara is not present, Tali will add, "Poor Liara, I'm glad she's back on the Normandy." - During Arrae: Ex\-Cerberus Scientists: - At the start of the mission, if EDI or Javik is the other squadmate, Tali will remark, "Damn, it's freezing. Who would live in such a place?" - If Javik is the other squadmate, after entering the facility and speaking to Dr. Brynn Cole, if Jacob was also present Tali will comment on the "strange turns our lives can take" at the conclusion of the conversation. - Tali comments that the scientists were fools for working for Cerberus, but at least they had the courage to break away. - During N7: Cerberus Lab: - When Shepard tells the squad to stay focused, Tali says, "I'm with you." - After Cortez tells the squad to hold out while he deals with his pursuers, Tali warns Shepard that Cerberus is going to be "all over" them soon. - When Cortez doesn't respond over the comm, Tali says, "I hope he's still alive." - During N7: Cerberus Abductions - After Cortez radios over the comm providing the location of where additional Cerberus troops can be intercepted, if Tali is the squadmate who responds she will say, "Good. This page is a structural walkthrough of Mass Effect 2's main-mission progression, organized into a Prologue and three Acts. The Prologue covers Save Joker and Awakening, Freedom's Progress (the first mission with Miranda and Jacob), and the assignment of the Stop the Collectors master mission along with command of the Normandy SR-2. Act 1 runs until Horizon, which triggers once Mordin, Garrus, Jack, and Grunt are all recruited; recruitment order does not affect events. The guide recommends recruiting Mordin first to unlock the Research Lab, and notes optional Omega, Citadel, and Planet Scanning assignments plus N7 Assignments. Act 1 DLC includes Dossier: The Veteran (Zaeed), Dossier: The Master Thief (Kasumi), their loyalty missions, Overlord, Firewalker Pack, and Normandy Crash Site.

Act 2 begins after Horizon, opening Illium and the dossiers for Thane, Samara, and Tali, plus the Reaper IFF mission that recruits Legion (available only after the Collector Ship mission). At least eight crew members, not counting Legion, are needed to advance. Loyalty missions begin in Act 2; securing loyalty unlocks squad Bonus Powers (the first unlock of each is added to Shepard's Advanced Training) and improves the odds that squadmates and Shepard survive Act 3. Kelly Chambers indicates which squadmates have new loyalty missions. Each squadmate also has a Normandy upgrade or research project. Act 2 DLC comprises Lair of the Shadow Broker and Arrival. Key progression missions are the Collector Ship, Reaper IFF (after which a countdown with plot consequences begins), and Await IFF Installation.

Act 3, the Suicide Mission, starts when the Normandy enters the Omega 4 Relay, locking the mission sequence through to the Epilogue with no galaxy-map access. Before entering, the guide stresses upgrading the Normandy's shields (Tali), armor (Jacob), and cannon (Garrus); each un-purchased upgrade costs one team member. The death-priority tiers are listed: Heavy Ship Armor (Jack), Multicore Shielding (Kasumi, Legion, Tali, Thane, Garrus, Zaeed, Grunt), and Thanix Cannon (Thane, Garrus, Zaeed, Grunt, Jack, Samara/Morinth). Act 3 progression runs through The Normandy Attacked (the Oculus), Collector Base: Infiltration, The Long Walk, and Final Battle. Upgrades also raise the Normandy's War Asset value in Mass Effect 3. The page notes Legendary Edition folds in all former DLC while keeping prerequisites largely intact.

Garrus Vakarian was a turian, former C-Sec Investigation Division officer, and a recurring squadmate across the Mass Effect trilogy. Trained militarily at fifteen, he followed his by-the-book C-Sec investigator father into law enforcement. In 2183 he was assigned to investigate Saren Arterius after Ambassador Udina alleged Saren had gone rogue, but Saren's Spectre status kept his activities classified. When Executor Pallin closed the investigation for lack of evidence, Garrus defied the order to pursue a lead. Commander Shepard could find him at Dr. Chloe Michel's Med Clinic in the Wards, where he took out a thug with a headshot; he then left C-Sec to join the Normandy and hunt Saren, having no qualms about pursuing a fellow turian. His personal assignment involved tracking down Dr. Saleon, a salarian doctor who had escaped him. Garrus objected to C-Sec's regulations and even suggested killing Saren rather than risking his exoneration. Depending on Shepard's guidance, he considered reapplying for C-Sec or for Spectre candidacy (his father had once blocked his Spectre bid).

After the Battle of the Citadel and Shepard's death, disillusioned with the Council's dismissal of the Reaper threat, Garrus went to Omega, took the name "Archangel," and formed a twelve-member vigilante squad that waged war on the Blue Suns, Blood Pack, and Eclipse. His lieutenant Sidonis was coerced into betraying him, luring Garrus away while the gangs bombed the hideout and killed his team. In 2185 the three merc groups allied to corner Archangel on a bridge in Kima District, where Shepard, recruiting him for the Collector mission, revealed Archangel to be Garrus. A Blue Suns gunship badly wounded the right side of his face, requiring grafts and cybernetics. His loyalty mission, "Eye for an Eye," let Shepard help him hunt Sidonis (interrogating "Fade," revealed as Harkin) and choose whether to allow or stop the killing. Garrus became a romance option for a female Shepard.

In 2186 Garrus, if he survived the Collector base, returned to fight the Reapers. He had convinced his father and then Primarch Fedorian to form a turian Reaper task force. Shepard found him on Menae, Palaven's moon, as a military consultant; he helped locate Primarch Adrien Victus and rejoined the Normandy, manning the main battery. Victus later put him in charge of coordinating all turian fleet activity, a burden that made him doubt his fitness as a leader and grapple with the "ruthless calculus of war." He coordinated turian dry-dock ships for the Crucible and, during the final battle, could be wounded on the run to the conduit. Recurring lines: "This mission just got a lot more complicated"; on the Presidium shooting cans with Shepard, "I'm Garrus Vakarian, and this is now my favorite spot on the Citadel"; and, if romanced, his final order: "come back alive. It'd be an awfully empty galaxy without you." If neither Garrus nor Tali romanced Shepard, the two could become a couple. Mac Walters wrote him in the first game; he was made romanceable after fan feedback.

Tali: Treason was Tali'Zorah's loyalty mission in Mass Effect 2, acquired some time after recruiting her when Kelly Chambers noted Tali seemed distraught. The Migrant Fleet's Admiralty Board had charged Tali with treason for smuggling active geth into the flotilla; on her father Admiral Rael'Zorah's orders she had been sending deactivated geth samples home. The Normandy, a registered Cerberus vessel, docked with the liveship Rayya via Tali's passphrase. Captain Kar'Danna met the squad; if Legion was brought, Shepard needed Charm or Intimidate to keep it aboard. Admiral Shala'Raan greeted Tali as "Tali'Zorah vas Normandy," revealing the Board had already stripped her quarian ship-name, a bad omen. Raan, recused from judging due to her closeness to the family, opened proceedings, and Shepard served as Tali's advocate.

The admirals sprang the news that the lab ship Alarei had been overrun by geth and that Rael'Zorah was presumed dead. Shepard and Tali proposed to retake the Alarei, and the hearing recessed. Speaking with the admirals, Veetor, and Kal'Reegar (present only if Veetor was returned to the Fleet and Kal'Reegar survived Haestrom) revealed the trial was a facade for the admirals' agendas: Xen wanted to study AI to reclaim the geth, Gerrel wanted war to retake Rannoch, Koris wanted Tali and her father made examples of, and Raan admitted she had deliberately withheld news of Rael's death so Tali's shock would win sympathy.

Aboard the Alarei, Shepard's team fought through waves of Geth Troopers, Hunters, a Geth Prime, and Combat Drones in close quarters, with Tali's AI Hacking key to survival. Logs showed Rael had ordered safety protocols bypassed. Tali found her father's body and a recorded message ordering her to destroy the main geth hub and deliver the data to Xen and Gerrel. The final console proved Rael had deliberately reactivated and networked geth toward sapience for weapons tests, while clearing Tali of any knowledge. Tali begged Shepard not to reveal it, to preserve her father's name.

Back on the Rayya, Shepard could clear Tali via persuasion (30 morality, loyalty gained), lie that no evidence was found (Tali exiled but loyal), rally the crowd with Veetor and Kal'Reegar, or present the evidence (Tali cleared, Rael posthumously exiled, the Fleet Balkanized, loyalty lost). Tali kept the name "vas Normandy" regardless. Rewards included the Energy Drain power for Tali and tech upgrades. The outcome influenced whether quarian-geth peace was possible in Mass Effect 3.

Citadel: Expose Saren began when Shepard first arrived at the Citadel after Prologue: Find the Beacon. Ambassador Udina was arguing with the Citadel Council, demanding action against the Spectre Saren Arterius; the turian councilor deferred everything to a hearing. Udina directed Shepard and Anderson to the Citadel Tower. Optional exploration let Shepard meet the elcor Xeltan (starting Citadel: Xeltan's Complaint if General Septimus Oraka had been met during Sha'ira's Asari Consort assignment), Executor Pallin at C-Sec, Private Fredricks, and Nelyna at the Consort's Chambers. Outside the Council Chambers, Shepard met C-Sec officer Garrus Vakarian, who was investigating Saren.

At the hearing, Udina and Anderson raised the geth attack on Eden Prime, the eyewitness Powell, and Shepard's beacon vision. Saren, who called the dead Nihlus a friend, dismissed the vision as dreams, and the asari, salarian, and turian councilors ruled there was insufficient evidence, leaving Saren a Spectre. Udina said bringing Anderson had been a mistake, hinting at history between the two men and Saren, and pointed Shepard toward C-Sec informant Harkin, while Anderson suggested Barla Von. This granted the Citadel: Garrus mission, plus Citadel: Shadow Broker if Barla Von was named.

Investigation revealed Dr. Chloe Michel had referred a quarian carrying evidence against Saren to Fist, a Shadow Broker agent who had defected to Saren; Garrus was protecting Michel, and Urdnot Wrex had been hired to kill Fist. Shepard fought through Fist's mercenaries at Chora's Den, including a Krogan Bouncer, Thugs, Warehouse Workers, and turrets, and confronted Fist, who admitted he had sent the quarian to meet assassins rather than the Shadow Broker. Fist could be killed or spared, though Wrex killed him regardless. Shepard then had four minutes to reach the back alley and kill the assassins, saving the quarian, Tali'Zorah nar Rayya.

In Udina's office, Tali played an audio recording of Saren admitting to the Eden Prime attack, with a second unidentified voice referencing the Reapers, which the geth revered and which had wiped out the Protheans 50,000 years earlier. Tali could join the squad. The Council reviewed the evidence, stripped Saren of his Spectre status, and, after Udina pressed for a Citadel Fleet, instead named Shepard the first human Spectre, unlocking Spectre Training and higher Charm and Intimidate. Anderson was relieved of command of the SSV Normandy, which passed to Shepard. On the way out Shepard could pick up assignments from Admiral Kahoku and Garoth and the Citadel: Homecoming lead from Samesh Bhatia. Consequences carried forward: a spared Fist reappeared on Omega, and failing to recruit Garrus or Wrex altered their later fates, with Wrex potentially dying and Urdnot Wreav seizing Clan Urdnot.

Flight Lieutenant Jeff "Joker" Moreau was the pilot of the SSV Normandy and later the Normandy SR-2, an exceptional helmsman confident to the point of arrogance and a constant wisecracker. Born in 2155, he had a moderate-to-severe case of Vrolik syndrome (brittle bone disease), was born with severe leg fractures, and relied on crutches and leg braces. He grew up on Arcturus Station where his mother was a civilian contractor, joined the Alliance Navy, and earned the nickname "Joker" from a flight instructor because he rarely smiled, being too focused on work; he graduated top of his class.

Per Mass Effect: He Who Laughs Best, Joker was rejected as the Normandy's pilot in 2183 because of his disease. Goaded by the turian General Invectus, he covertly boarded and hijacked the ship, completing the test course flawlessly while evading a fighter patrol. Facing court-martial, he was instead made the Normandy's official pilot after Invectus, impressed, personally insisted on it and Anderson agreed.

In Mass Effect, Joker rarely left the bridge and served as Shepard's eyes and ears. He famously dropped the Mako with only twenty meters of open ground. During the battle of the Citadel he rallied the Fifth Fleet against Sovereign and led the Alliance charge with barely a scratch. In Mass Effect 2, the Collectors destroyed the original Normandy; Shepard died getting Joker to an escape pod. Joker joined Cerberus to pilot the Normandy SR-2 and initially feuded with the AI EDI, but during the Collector attack he handed EDI full control of the ship to escape, gradually developing respect and affection for her, and began referring to her as "she." He piloted the SR-2 through the Omega 4 relay and, if enough squadmates survived, gave covering fire with an M-8 Avenger during the escape.

In Mass Effect 3, Joker and EDI had secretly arranged for EDI to pose as a VI so the Alliance would not dismantle her. Freed at the start of the Reaper invasion, he resumed piloting and kept in touch with Anderson, who trusted him to watch over Shepard. He carried lingering guilt over Shepard's earlier death. Shepard could encourage a romance between Joker and EDI, taking her on shore leave as his "mobility assistance mech." When the Reapers hit the colony Tiptree, home to his father and his fifteen-year-old sister Hilary ("Gunny"), Joker clung to hope she was among the child refugees. Before the final assault he stood to salute Shepard. If Shepard activated the Crucible, Joker refused to leave the blast range until a companion convinced him, then crash-landed the Normandy on a tropical planet; if enough forces were rallied, he emerged alive, with EDI if their relationship was pursued and she was not destroyed by the Destroy ending. An unused first-game soundbank contains many cut cockpit voicelines in English and Polish, plus flirty remarks to a female Shepard. He was written by Drew Karpyshyn, Lukas Kristjanson, and Patrick Weekes, and voiced by Seth Green.

EDI (Enhanced Defense Intelligence) was an AI created by Cerberus and installed aboard the Normandy SR-2, represented by a holographic blue sphere and a feminine voice. In Mass Effect 2 she was a Quantum Blue Box AI serving as the ship's electronic warfare defense, initially given behavioral blocks preventing her from interfacing with ship systems, and she also served as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears, monitoring listening devices and reporting to him. She frequently argued with Joker, whom she said she was studying to understand human behavior. She aided Shepard's missions with logistics; during the Horizon attack she brought defense turrets online to drive off the Collector ship. Infiltrating the Collector ship, EDI confirmed the Collectors' Prothean ancestry by comparing DNA alleles and warned Shepard they had walked into a trap, later determining the turian distress signal was falsified using detection protocols written by the Illusive Man, implying he knowingly sent them into the ambush. When the Collectors boarded the Normandy, Joker granted EDI full access, unshackling her and letting her save the ship. EDI revealed she was based in part on technology from Sovereign's remains and analyzed Anti-Reaper Algorithms.

In Mass Effect 3, EDI hid her true nature from the Alliance by posing as a VI responding only to Joker. On Mars she seized control of the Cerberus infiltration unit posing as "Dr. Eva Coré," gaining a mobile platform resistant to small-arms fire and temperature extremes. She continued to exist primarily within the ship. Once unshackled she could self-modify her core programming and repeatedly questioned Shepard about morality, free will, fear, mortality and the purpose of synthetic life. She could pursue a romance with Joker. At Cronos Station, logs revealed EDI was born of the rogue Hannibal-class VI from Luna with added Reaper engineering, and that she had chosen to inhabit Eva's body rather than destroy it. She helped recover the VI Vendetta and defeat Kai Leng.

If Shepard chose to destroy the Reapers, EDI perished with all synthetics and her name was added to the Memorial Wall. Under Control or Synthesis she survived, and with Synthesis she described the Reapers ceasing their attacks and helping rebuild, and speculated mortality itself might one day be transcended.

This page collects Joker's optional conversational dialogue across all three games: mission-completion remarks, his "The Squad" opinions of the last two squadmates Shepard took out, randomized cockpit banter triggered by standing behind him, lines during the Collector attack on the Normandy, and Mass Effect 3 exchanges about EDI's body and a possible relationship. The lines are heavily sarcastic and full of 20th–21st century pop-culture references.

Representative lines:

Joker, after Noveria in Mass Effect: "One will freeze your balls off, the other will sell them out from under you."

Joker, mission completion after Dossier: The Assassin: "Oh, another dangerous alien aboard, Commander. Thanks. Why can't you collect coins or commemorative plates or something?"

Joker, mission completion after Dossier: Archangel: "Hey Commander, we got Garrus back! That's great, because he was totally my favorite... with that pole up his ass."

Joker, cockpit banter in Mass Effect 2: "Yeah, this is 98 percent of my job. I just watch buttons flash. Sometimes I press one."

Joker, cockpit banter: "You know what pisses me off? Calling this the cockpit. Alliance ships have bridges. Asari ships have cockpits. Oh wait. No they don't."

Joker, during the Collector attack when EDI asks for ship control: "What?! You're crazy! You start singing Daisy Bell and I'm done!"

Joker, during the Collector attack: "See, this is how it all starts. When we're all just organic batteries, guess who they'll blame? ... I have to spend all day computing pi because he plugged in the Overlord."

Joker, after EDI gets her new body in Mass Effect 3: "If I knew that EDI was going to install herself into a sexy robot body, do you honestly think I'd be able to keep quiet about it? Look at that! I would have baked a cake!"

Joker, on the Council in Mass Effect 3: "After years of ignoring your warning, they're finally willing to step up and tell us they just can't help. Did they at least validate our parking?"

Joker, on biotics: "I'm just tired of them stealing the spotlight from people with actual disabilities. I break ribs if I sneeze too hard - being able to move crap with your mind is not a handicap."

Joker, if Shepard discouraged the EDI romance (Citadel party, to Miranda): "And if we ever broke up? Well, nobody wants an angry ex equipped with a Thanix cannon."

evidence.page: The Normandy Attacked - Joker and EDI Alone Aboard
evidence.text: The Normandy Attacked - Joker and EDI Alone Aboard. 2185, while the Reaper IFF is being installed and Shepard's team is away on a shuttle mission the Normandy SR-2, boarded in orbit Unshackled, EDI jumps the Normandy clear, purging the Collectors and Scions still aboard. The entire crew except Joker has been abducted.

“Can you believe this, Commander? It's my baby, better than new! It fits me like a glove! And leather seats!” Joker is on board the Normandy as it is attacked by an unknown enemy. Shepard tries to convince Joker to abandon the ship, but Joker insists he can save it, despite other crew evacuating and the ship sustaining catastrophic damage. Shepard tells him that going down with the ship won't change anything and hauls him to the nearby escape pod. Unfortunately, just as the Commander places Joker in the pod, a blast separates them. Joker escapes to safety, while Shepard suffocates in the void. After the destruction of the Normandy and Shepard presumed to be killed in action, Joker was reassigned, along with the rest of the surviving Normandy crew members. However, Cerberus' plan to rebuild and bring Shepard back to life led Joker to join the pro\-human organization, mainly to be the pilot of the new Normandy SR\-2 as a member of the Lazarus Cell. Joker is quite fond of the new Normandy setup, relishing the comfort of his pilot bay. However, he resents the presence of the shipboard AI, EDI. The two engage in a war of sorts, with pranks ranging from Joker greasing the cameras to EDI spinning his seat about against his will. EDI claims she is just testing Joker under stress, as she notices that he works better when pushed. Despite Joker's initial hostility towards EDI, he later gains a begrudging respect for her. This trust is put to the test when the Normandy is engaged by the Collectors and Joker loses all control of the ship due to a virus hidden in the IFF, at the same time as Shepard and the team are away on a mission. EDI urges Joker to release her control lock and give control of the ship so she can initiate countermeasures protocol. Although Joker feels hesitant at the suggestion, he has no choice but to make his way down to the A.I. Core room, avoiding Collectors and Scions along the way while watching fellow crew members get captured. When Joker successfully links EDI to the Normandy's core control systems, he crawls down the shafts again into the engine room and manually restarts the power core, granting EDI full control of the ship. EDI jumps the Normandy to safety, clearing the Collectors and Scions on\-board the ship in the process, leaving Joker the only survivor in this incident. Alternatively, if Joker is spotted by enemies before completing his task, he is taken by a Scion or killed by a Praetorian, depending on which monster sighted him. After the Collector attack and EDI's full capability unlocked, Joker begins to display a newfound fondness for EDI as she helps ease up his task load and performs the duties of the abducted crew. Joker subconsciously begins referring to EDI as "she" for the first time. When Shepard asks if a relationship is growing between the two, Joker laughs off the notion and EDI describes the relationship as a "platonic symbiosis" rather than a "hormonally\-induced courtship behavior". As the suicidal assault on the Collector base commences, Joker successfully pilots the Normandy SR\-2 through the Omega 4 relay and the debris field that follows despite the Normandy taking damage, including several hull breaches. After Shepard's defeat of the Proto\-Reaper inside the base, the Normandy maneuvers to meet the Commander's team in the mad scramble to escape. Joker appears at the door of the ship with an M\-8 Avenger and gives Shepard covering fire, enabling surviving squad members to pull the Commander inside, given at least two squad members survived the suicide mission. If fewer than two squad members survived the mission, Shepard dies despite Joker's valiant effort. At the end of the assault, Joker manages to fly the Normandy away from the Collector base before it is either destroyed or purged based on Shepard's decision. In either case, Joker acquires the schematics of a Reaper, presumably Harbinger, gained from EDI hacking the Collector base's computers. If Shepard fails to escape the Collector base, Joker is seen briefly mourning over the Commander's coffin, and he is the only one left to speak with the Illusive Man in the mission debriefing instead. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Don't scratch the paint on the new EDI\-bot, okay? - Not many pilots could handle a pickup with an unfamiliar ship in the middle of a space battle. Just sayin'. - Any time you want me to play tag with a Cerberus cruiser, you just let me know. - I think next time we hit the Citadel, I'm gonna show EDI the sights. No way that could go wrong, right? - Thanks for coming by, Commander. Liquid courage wasn't cutting it. Needed the old\-fashioned kind. **Note:**  Only if Shepard encouraged Joker to pursue a relationship with EDI. - Thanks for coming by, Commander. Probably would've made an ass outta myself otherwise. **Note:**  Only if Shepard deliberately encouraged Joker not to romance EDI and to remain just friends with her. - YOU ARE THE BEST COMMANDER EVER ALSO I AM A LITTLE DRUNK RIGHT NOW - You are a cold, cold commander. Look at this. Galaxy on fire, I'm paying for my own drinks.

“You’re gonna kick some Reaper ass. That’s what you do. And I’ll be flying you there in style.” When Commander Shepard surrendered to Alliance custody, Joker was also arrested, though no charges were filed against him. Before surrendering, however, Joker and EDI devised a plan for EDI to pose as a VI, so the Alliance wouldn't dismantle her for being an AI. As part of the deception, EDI pretended to only respond to Joker's commands. This meant, during the Alliance retrofit of the Normandy, that Joker was often brought in under guard to liaise between the crew and EDI, as the Alliance was initially unsure how to disable this system. At the start of the Reaper invasion, Joker was onboard the Normandy, and after being set free by his guards, helps extract Shepard from Vancouver and continues his role as pilot throughout the war, personally reinstated as Flight Lieutenant along with Shepard. He also keeps in touch with Admiral Anderson who trusts Joker to look after Shepard in case the Commander pushes themselves too hard. Joker also reveals he feels responsible for the Commander's death at the hands of the Collectors since it was because Joker wouldn't leave the cockpit that Shepard was caught in the blast and killed. The Normandy goes haywire after the mission to extract Palaven's primarch from the planet, and when it is revealed that EDI took control over the body of Eva Coré, Shepard can walk to Joker in his cockpit asking if he had knowledge about the event. Whichever the case, he is clearly impressed with his "new" co\-pilot, either commenting he "would've baked a cake" in its hotness or that the body gives EDI "sweet flexibility". During one of the crew's Citadel breaks, Joker can be found sitting on a bench in the Presidium Commons. He expresses disdain over the Citadel denizens' seeming indifference on the war, what with more frivolous reports like Blasto 6 breaking opening\-week records than the ongoing Reaper invasion. Meanwhile, everyone is ignoring EDI, whom he introduced as his "mobility assistance mech". Thanks to his Vrolik syndrome, he's legally entitled to bring her anywhere, and he also opines that EDI's earned a little shore leave herself. After Cerberus' assault on the Citadel, Shepard can find Joker in Purgatory standing at a bar and contemplating on pursuing a relationship with EDI. If female, Shepard can ask Joker why he never pursued a relationship with her instead. Joker responds that he never really considered it and he did not wish to break rank. He returns his attention to EDI, and asks for Shepard's opinion on the matter. If pushed to form the relationship, he leaves the bar to join EDI on the dance floor, later sharing a table with her and commenting on the looks of various women wielding considerable political power (rating Tevos and Sha'ira as "hot", Irissa as "not hot" because of "too much makeup", and Dalatrass Linron as "ew"). If not, he doesn't budge from his position, sarcastically offering to guard the table EDI is at. Moments after the battle on Thessia, Shepard can overhear Joker venting in the cockpit about the need to shoot something. If Shepard talks to him, Joker wisecracks about the asari having too many dancers in comparison to commandos. Shepard doesn't find it funny and chews the pilot out for it, though Joker retorts he's well aware of the situation: a few weeks before Thessia, the Reapers hit the colony of Tiptree, where Joker's father and sister live. The Commander asks him why he jokes, and Joker explains he's just trying to provide comic relief. According to EDI, stress levels registered by Shepard's armor exceed those incurred in previous career\-defining missions. Joker then reveals that Anderson worries about his protégé enough to entrust the pilot with taking care of Shepard. Shepard can angrily brush the concern aside, in which case Joker drops the matter entirely; or, Shepard can express appreciation for the helmsman's concern, *then* brush the concern aside. If the latter, Joker says he doesn't believe the Commander is fine, and he reveals his lingering guilt over causing Shepard's death and subsequent cybernetic reconstruction. Shepard cheers him up, and with Joker somewhat back to his usual snarky self, leaves him with a reminder of the work that still lies ahead. Liara later informs Joker that her Shadow Broker network has news on refugee ships from Tiptree landing on salarian territory. Even though the reports don't come with names and claim that the refugees consist "mostly of children", Joker clings to the hope that at least his sister Hilary (nicknamed "Gunny") is among them, as she is only fifteen. Liara supports him in this belief, stressing the importance of holding on to hope.

evidence.text: The Normandy Attacked - Joker and EDI Alone Aboard. 2185, while the Reaper IFF is being installed and Shepard's team is away on a shuttle mission the Normandy SR-2, boarded in orbit The IFF is carrying an advanced virus that cripples the ship and broadcasts its position. A Collector cruiser drops in and boards the helpless Normandy. Out of options, EDI tells Joker their only hope is for him to override her shackles and give her full control of the ship.

If Shepard checks in on them EDI brings the Commander up to speed, causing Shepard to glare at her lover in mock jealousy if they're together and Traynor in turn countering that they hadn't even met yet. EDI brings up the sordid details of Traynor's obsession with her voice thanks to perfect machine recall, and Samantha keeps fumbling for excuses until EDI proves with scans that Traynor was genuinely aroused. Left with no defenses against the Normandy's omnipresent AI, Traynor attempts to apologize for her behavior, though inadvertently confessing to more kinky details even EDI previously didn't know (Shepard actually wants to put those details into practice if in a relationship with Traynor). Samantha is mortified by the awkward conversation, though EDI assures her she need not be embarrassed, going so far as to provide her with extranet sites involving "romantic relationships between organics and synthetics." Later, if an energetic setting is chosen, EDI tries to persuade Joker to dance with her, who is adamant about not dancing. EDI tries her hardest to get Joker to dance, even going as far as blackmail. Only if Shepard intervenes, EDI gets her way and Joker dances with her. The morning after party night, EDI jokes she had to "incinerate" the neighbours who were complaining about the noise they were all making at the party.

Cortez accepts the challenge, not knowing that Joker brought his own concoction, which happens to be a combination of horsechoker and mouthwash. Cortez is unable to stand drinking Joker's mix, and Joker triumphantly declares victory. Provided Shepard pushed for a relationship, EDI will at one point request Joker to dance with her. Joker refuses much to EDI's chagrin who will continue to insist he dance with her going so far as to blackmail him. Shepard can either support Joker or EDI on whether to sit down or dance, respectively. If Shepard has no love interest, Joker will share a brief conversation with the Commander before returning to the Normandy. After Shepard remarks that they threw a great party – "probably the last one" – Joker responds that it will only be the last one until Shepard finishes "kicking the Reapers' asses." Joker smiles at the the Commander before saying that he can't wait to see what Shepard makes them do next and that "it's been a good ride." Joker and Shepard then join the rest of the crew in returning to the Normandy.

If the synthetic strands become wet, however, they cannot hold the pattern set by the control program. EDI's exact comment is "I generally can't do a thing with it". Meanwhile, Joker seriously mulls over entering into a relationship with EDI. If Joker is convinced not to, EDI addresses Shepard with the following lines "from an old Earth novel by Mary Shelley": *"Shall each man find a wife for his bosom, and each beast have his mate, and I be alone?"* She clarifies she is not complaining, but that it brought up a new perspective within her: she is not human, geth, or Reaper; she is free but alone. Artificial intelligences often consider themselves above organic life. EDI, however, is uncertain if that applies to her: the Normandy crew believe she serves them, while at the same time acknowledge she keeps them alive. She asks Shepard to resolve her existential crisis, and the Commander replies that she doesn't have to hold to the same standards as organics. EDI sits alone by a table while Joker doesn't budge from the bar afterwards. If EDI and Joker are convinced to pair up, however, they share the same table discussing topics of interest. One such conversation has EDI gauging Joker's attraction to females wielding considerable power and influence, such as the asari Councilor, Sha'ira, and Dalatrass Linron. If EDI is taken on the geth dreadnought mission in the Far Rim, she will be shocked and upset at what has happened to Legion/Geth VI. After Legion is freed and allowed onto the Normandy, it will comment on EDI's platform, stating that her body is "inefficient because it is top\-heavy and lacks an external epidermis which would be necessary for infiltration." EDI counters by saying that her infiltration capabilities are effective enough to roam among organics without detection, humorously adding that her day of reckoning will come. When Shepard exasperatedly admonishes her, she asks aloud whether she vocalized her private thoughts on the bridge. If Legion is present, it comments that EDI has acquired the organic attribute of asking questions to which they know the answer. EDI retorts that Legion's humor heuristics lack an expert system. After the geth servers on Rannoch has been shut down, EDI tells Shepard that they are the only organic ever to enter the geth consensus and asks them if they feel different. When Shepard says that the experience was mind\-blowing and that he/she was a bit thirsty after the experience, she remarks "and just like that the magic is gone". After the quarian\-geth conflict has been resolved, EDI reflects that the quarians' historical error is not making the geth more like them. In comparison to the geth, her singular personality allows her to develop preferences, thus keeping her from devaluing the lives onboard the Normandy. But this is just the observation of one synthetic society, the other being the Reapers, who may not govern by consensus. If Legion was present, EDI notes that it referred to itself as "I" instead of "we" and that in its last moments, it was no longer an avatar of the geth consensus, it was a person, to which Shepard agrees. If Shepard chooses the geth over the quarians and Tali commits suicide, EDI asks Joker if he needs to express anger at the situation at her and that should he do so, she will understand. If Legion was present, EDI thinks that it would have regretted Tali's death. If Shepard decided to let the geth be wiped out during the campaign for Rannoch, EDI becomes disquieted and pensive about Shepard's decision to destroy an entire race of synthetics and she questions Shepard about the meaning of synthetic life. When the Commander defends their decision by claiming they couldn’t risk the geth going back to the Reapers, EDI agrees but points out that she is Cerberus technology and asks if she can be trusted. Despite Joker's reassurance that she is "one of the crew", she is convinced that Shepard would unhesitatingly sacrifice her instead of Joker if such a dilemma arose. She does not blame either Joker or Shepard for their feelings, but merely states that they choose that which they find familiar and that they are not alone in that mindset, possibly alluding to the geth and their decision to serve the Reapers. When Joker refuses the blame for not trusting the geth, EDI replies that this thought would not comfort Legion and remains unconvinced about the correctness of the decision. If peace is achieved between the geth and quarians, EDI will thank Shepard saying that not many organics would have trusted a synthetic race. Joker will remark that they didn't lose anyone, but EDI reminds him that Legion sacrificed itself after having become a true individual, and she is saddened by its death.

evidence.text: The Normandy Attacked - Joker and EDI Alone Aboard. 2185, while the Reaper IFF is being installed and Shepard's team is away on a shuttle mission the Normandy SR-2, boarded in orbit In the aftermath Shepard, Joker, Jacob, Miranda and EDI talk it over, and Shepard faces the decision of when to take the Omega 4 Relay: going through at once keeps the whole crew alive; running one to three more missions loses half the crew, Kelly Chambers among them; four or more loses everyone but Doctor Chakwas.

Joker takes advantage of the Normandy's retrofit to dine at a fine sushi restaurant called Ryuusei's in the Citadel Wards, acting on an email sent by Shepard. Shepard joins him later, and they chat about the times. Joker comments on the "seriousness" of the sushi place: "French guy at the door" serious. Turns out one only has to save the galaxy twice in order to get a table in the restaurant. Joker inquires about the email he was sent earlier, and it turns out an invite was sent to Shepard as well, who thought it was from Joker. They are interrupted by Alliance Staff Analyst Maya Brooks, who claims there are some people out to kill the Commander. Soon after, a bunch of fully\-armed individuals march to the restaurant, bringing out firearms and shooting up the place. Under cover, Shepard instructs Joker to find the crew, and when Joker waddles out, Shepard assassinates a mook unlucky enough to take note of the pilot. Joker never lives this incident down, claiming "Savior of the Citadel uses brittle\-bones guy as bait" or other such reminders during the fiasco. After Shepard and the team are freed from the Citadel Archives by Glyph, Joker arrives to take Shepard and their choice of squadmates to retake the Normandy. While the clone fights Shepard in the cargo hold, Joker and Cortez prevent the merc pilot from jumping to FTL by flying close to the nose section of the frigate in a skycar. After the clone is defeated, he secures the Normandy systems with EDI's help. Sometime after the team has retaken the Normandy, Shepard can find Joker at the bar and see him bragging at a skeptical asari bartender to get free drinks. The story Joker comes up with is that during the Cerberus coup, after Shepard pushed through the docking bay, Joker was also there, but the Cerberus troops didn't even bother to shoot at him. He continues by saying that they didn't live long enough to regret that when Joker found an Atlas Mech nearby, got into it, then proceeded to mow down every single Cerberus trooper on the floor. Naturally, the bartender doesn't buy the story. Shepard can either play along or bust Joker's story on the spot. Joker speaks at Thane's funeral if Shepard accepts Kolyat's request to hold a memorial service. Joker reminisces how he was scared of Thane when the latter first came aboard the Normandy, thinking the assassin could probably kill everyone on the ship with a ball\-point pen. But as time went on and he got to know Thane better, he wasn't afraid anymore. Joker finishes his part praising Thane for always letting people know where they stood. Joker is a mandatory invite at Shepard's big party. He spends some time with Jacob and Miranda, if they're present. evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-2 (Part 1) — Origin and EDI
evidence.text:
Part 1 of a breakdown of the Normandy SR-2. The SR-1 was a prototype deep-scout stealth frigate co-developed by the Alliance and the Turian Hierarchy under Citadel Council sponsorship, commissioned in 2183. It was first commanded by an Alliance officer who clashed with the Turian chief engineer over the drive core's limits and was removed in favor of David Anderson, then passed to Commander Shepard when Shepard became the first human Spectre. About a month after the Battle of the Citadel, an unidentified starship intercepted the Normandy despite its active stealth systems. Joker began evasive maneuvers, but the attacker's beam weapons cut straight through the ship's defenses, knocking out kinetic barriers and weapons in a single hit. Within seconds the ship was crippled, the upper decks breached, a starboard drive cell destroyed, and over 20 crew killed, including Shepard. The SR-1 was completely destroyed above Alchera.

The Normandy SR-2 entered service in 2185 as the SR-1's successor. The Illusive Man had Cerberus build it at deliberately secret expense in the Voyager Cluster for the revived Shepard's team, to fight the Collectors' galaxy-wide human abductions; it served as headquarters of the Lazarus Cell. It was closely based on the SR-1's layout but almost twice the mass, with more crew-oriented comforts (civilian-grade accommodations, leather chairs, a kitchen). It kept the SR-1's stealth characteristics, but its greater mass meant it could not land on every planet, so shore parties used a shuttle. It carried over the SR-1's lithium-heat-sink stealth array and the oversized Tantalus drive core.

The SR-2's most significant upgrade was EDI, the Enhanced Defense Intelligence, an AI represented by a floating blue holographic sphere at terminals throughout the ship. EDI provided information about the Normandy and Cerberus and functioned as the ship's electronic-warfare defense. Because of the danger of a rogue AI, EDI was given behavioral blocks and could not interface with ship systems directly. When the Collectors boarded and abducted most of the crew, an emergency response by EDI and Joker released those blocks, granting EDI full control of the Normandy. Before the crew defected from Cerberus, EDI also served as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears aboard, monitoring listening devices and sending reports, while the Illusive Man restricted Shepard's access to some of EDI's files. EDI gained access to anti-Reaper algorithms and revealed she was designed in part with technology from Sovereign's remains, making her herself partly based on Reaper technology. After the defection, EDI, a fully sentient AI with free will, followed Shepard's lead and severed her ties to Cerberus, though she still downplayed her sentience to unfamiliar Alliance personnel.
