This page collects the squad barks, conversation lines, and spontaneous remarks Urdnot Wrex delivers when he is in Commander Shepard's squad, drawn from Mass Effect and Mass Effect 3 (including the Citadel DLC). The lines showcase his bluntness, love of violence, contempt for turians and salarians, and pride in fallen krogan glory. Representative quotes:

Wrex, when Shepard spares the warehouse workers during Citadel: Expose Saren: "It would've been quicker to just to kill them."

Wrex, to Executor Pallin claiming he never bends the law: "Don't piss in my ear and tell me it's raining, I've known plenty of dirty C-Sec agents."

Wrex, meeting the Thorian on Feros: "And they call *me* ugly..."

Wrex, opening negotiations with the Rachni Queen at Peak 15: "This is going to be a fun conversation."

Wrex, to the Mira VI when it insists neutron radiation is lethal to all known life: "I won't have some virtual wench questioning my fitness!"

Wrex, if brought without Garrus on Garrus: Find Dr. Saleon: "If you're too weak to hunt, you don't deserve the kill."

Wrex, at the Krogan Monument on the Presidium: "This statue represents what the krogan use to be: a proud and fierce nation. Now we're just brutes for hire to the highest bidder. We've forgotten our roots."

Wrex, to Tali at the Krogan Monument: "At least you still live. In another two hundred years, this statue may be the only evidence my people ever existed."

Wrex, on Therum's surface: "Fifty degrees hotter and I might start to feel uncomfortable. How are you mammals doing, Shepard?"

Wrex, on Ilos: "There's something in the air here; death is on the wind. It's a good place for killing."

Wrex, distracting a guard during Silver Coast Casino: Infiltration: "I need to look at your kitchen. I'm a food inspector."

Wrex, after the squad guns down Shepard's pursuers in Citadel Archives: Escape: "That's why I love hanging out with you guys! Why shoot something once when you can shoot it 46 more times?"

Wrex, trapped in the vault with Shepard: "Refresh my memory. Didn't we used to win these things back in the old days?"

Wrex, in combat during Mass Effect 3: "Uncle Urdnot has a present for you!"

Wrex, if Shepard talks Brooks into surrender during Retake the Normandy: "In the old days, we would have just shot her. Good times."

The page also notes recurring bits: Wrex and Garrus argue in Citadel elevators about the genophage and about whether Shepard or Saren would win a fight, and Wrex repeatedly disdains bars that want to hire krogan bouncers "as a status symbol."

Emilio Vega was James Vega's uncle and a father figure who lived in Escondido, California, and encouraged James to join the Systems Alliance Marines. Before James's mother died she made Emilio promise to look out for her son. Emilio helped James enlist in 2176. After James argued with his father, Joshua Sanders, and feared Josh would report to the military that James had bought drugs for him in San Diego, Emilio reassured him that Josh would never admit to a drug deal made through a minor, and told James that only he could choose how to live his life. James went on to join the Alliance. During the Reaper invasion of 2186, James sought news of his father and uncle, both still on Earth, but Citadel authorities could not contact them.

Lakshmi was a street urchin in the Terminus Systems featured in Mass Effect: Foundation. A brunette girl almost ten years old with a distinctive Y-shaped scar over her right eye, she came from an impoverished background and begged in the streets to survive. She encountered Miranda Lawson and Jacob Taylor; Miranda gave her nothing, but Jacob promised credits for directions. Lakshmi warned them the place they sought was dangerous, as her cousin's family had been abducted there and enslaved, and when batarian thugs attacked she lured the pair to safety and gave them decorated red and green fabrics to mask their faces.

Later, a batarian food vendor took her credits but refused her the leg meat she wanted, accusing her of theft, before a piece of a crashing Cerberus ship killed him and destroyed the stall. Another batarian shoved her and demanded she fetch her uncle Taleed. When an injured Jacob came looking for Miranda, Lakshmi helped him, warned off hoodlums with her uncle's reputation, and reluctantly revealed she knew where Miranda was being held. Her mother had her prepare a bed for Jacob, and Lakshmi later showed him her uncle's weapons stash when he vowed to rescue her enslaved aunt and cousins. She guided him to the slavers' warehouse, where she saw her uncle ordered to kill Miranda and was herself seized as a hostage by the batarian ringleader Torthak. Jacob shot the batarian and freed her; her family, minus her uncle, was reunited. Lakshmi hugged Jacob in gratitude and gave Miranda a yellow rose before running off.

With that knowledge, James successfully joined the Alliance and became a Marine.

Joshua Sanders was James Vega's father. After the death of his wife, Josh's relationship with his son became strained and he began using red sand. He lived in a beach house in Solana Beach, California.

Liara T'Soni is tracking down the mysterious Shadow Broker, and no one is safe. She'll do anything to recover the man the Broker kidnapped... and the Shadow Broker's agents will do anything to stop her. Team up with Liara and chase clues from the luxurious heights of Illium to the Shadow Broker's own secret lair. This DLC adds the Shadow Broker intel center, new research, and five new achievements – and the chance to continue a relationship with Liara.

In 2185, the Shadow Broker is being pursued by Liara T'Soni due to Feron's capture. Unbeknownst to Liara, the Broker has a double agent in her employ named Nyxeris to monitor her progress and, when possible, to kill her. It is also heavily implied by Liara that the Shadow Broker is an individual. Thane Krios also mentions that some years ago, batarian mercenaries employed the Shadow Broker to learn Thane's identity, and later used this information to murder his wife, Irikah.

*Main article: Lair of the Shadow Broker (mission)* Shepard is sent information on the Shadow Broker obtained by Cerberus. Shepard travels back to Illium and passes this information onto Liara, who examines it and determines that Feron is indeed alive, and in the custody of the Shadow Broker. After surviving an assassination attempt by a rogue Spectre working for the Shadow Broker, Tela Vasir, Liara, with assistance from Shepard and the information obtained from Cerberus, travels to the Shadow Broker Base on the planet Hagalaz. There, they find Feron being tortured for his previous betrayal of the Broker. Unable to remove the drell from the device holding him down without killing him, Liara and Shepard confront the Shadow Broker, killing him in the process. Now free from the Shadow Broker's custody, Feron opts to remain in the Shadow Broker's base so he can assist Liara, who has taken over as Shadow Broker following the previous Broker's death. He remains unsure what he will do afterward. Liara expresses great concern for Feron, worried his ordeal has left him mentally scarred. In conversation with Shepard, he mentions using his drell ability to slip into old memories to escape the torture. Shepard can ask Liara if she is romantically involved with Feron, and her answers will differ slightly depending on whether or not Shepard is in a relationship with Liara, but both result in Liara denying it. However, her response is somewhat ambiguous if Shepard is not romancing Liara. She points out that at this time, Feron is too emotionally unstable for a relationship and that it would be irresponsible "to take advantage" of the situation. Asking Feron about his relationship with Liara will result in him saying that Liara is a far better friend than he deserves. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

“I know your every secret, while you fumble in the dark.” *Main article: Lair of the Shadow Broker (mission)* If Commander Shepard obtains certain information from Cerberus, the opportunity to team up with Liara T'Soni to confront the Shadow Broker appears. #### Identity After tracking down and infiltrating the Shadow Broker's ship, Shepard and Liara break into the Broker's intel center and confront him in person. The Shadow Broker is revealed to be a member of a pre\-spaceflight race called the yahg. Liara surmises that because the yahg were not discovered until 2125 CE and the Broker's ship is considerably older than that, this yahg usurped the original Shadow Broker years ago and has been running the organization ever since. In the Dossiers terminal found in the ship's intel center, a personal file about the Shadow Broker can be read. The file's messages reveal that after the yahg's homeworld Parnack was discovered and then declared off\-limits in 2125 CE, the original Shadow Broker had his operatives abduct a yahg for him to study. The captured yahg proved highly intelligent and adaptable. With the Shadow Broker's support, the yahg killed the operative that was monitoring him and assumed the operative's identity, attaining a high rank within the organization as "Operative Kechlu". Sometime later, the Shadow Broker became aware that "Operative Kechlu" was a threat and attempted to eliminate him, but was beaten to the chase by "Kechlu". The yahg seamlessly took on the role of Shadow Broker and maintained the organization for the next six decades. #### Future Plans At some point during his reign, the Shadow Broker became aware of the Reapers and the true nature of the Collectors. Liara T'Soni suggests his dealings with the Collectors were a selfish and ill\-conceived attempt to ensure his own survival from the Reapers' coming genocide. Ultimately, the Shadow Broker was never given the chance to further his plans. #### Fate Liara, Shepard, and a third teammate attempt to battle the Shadow Broker in his own office. The Broker manages to incapacitate the third squadmate before the fight even begins. It takes Shepard and Liara extensive teamwork to catch the yahg off guard, turning his own kinetic technology against him as he dies in a fiery explosion. With the death of the yahg Broker, Liara T'Soni steps into the role of Shadow Broker herself. As Shepard and Liara had killed the few operatives aware of the Broker's true identity, Liara could take over without anyone else in the organization suspecting a transition. Liara is well aware of the power at her disposal, capable of starting a war in ten minutes if she wanted to, but vows to not abuse her position and to help Shepard find a way to combat the Reapers. |  | ***“You've got to walk your own path...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Homeworlds** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

If Liara succeeded in saving Feron from the Shadow Broker, following the destruction of the Shadow Broker Base in 2186, Liara tasks Feron with tracking Tazzik down. According to Feron, Tazzik is none too pleased to learn that he has to take orders from Feron, but he complies and acts as a bodyguard for Feron and a group of Shadow Broker agents as they travel through the Terminus Systems to gather intel. Tazzik is unaware of Liara's place as the new Shadow Broker and it can be inferred that he assumes that nothing has changed, aside from Feron becoming an asset instead of a liability.

Feron was a drell information trafficker who described himself as "an information trader. Not a slaver." In Mass Effect: Redemption, set after the destruction of the Normandy SR-1, Liara T'Soni hired him to help find Commander Shepard; he reported that Shepard was neither dead nor alive. Ambushed by Blue Suns sent by the Shadow Broker to delay Liara, the pair were saved by an unknown sniper, then encountered Cerberus agents, including Miranda Lawson, and were brought to the Illusive Man, who revealed the Shadow Broker was working with the Collectors. Feron admitted he had been ordered to lead Liara away from Shepard but chose to help her instead.

Feron took Liara to Afterlife on Omega, where Aria T'Loak resided, and learned where the Blue Suns would bring Shepard's body. He spotted the Broker's enforcer Tazzik but missed his ship with a turret, letting Tazzik flee Omega with the body. Feron revealed he had never stopped working for the Shadow Broker, which they could exploit to track Tazzik. The two infiltrated the Broker's base on Alingon, with Feron passing Liara off as his prisoner; he downloaded the Broker's dealings while Liara distracted a hologram of the Broker. Feron confessed Cerberus had recruited him and that he and the Illusive Man had planned for Feron to snatch the body. When a Collector exposed him as a traitor, Feron held off Tazzik so Liara could escape, and was captured.

In Mass Effect 2, Liara mentioned a "friend" lost during her search. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, Liara, Shepard, and Cerberus intel led to the Shadow Broker Base on Hagalaz, where Feron was found being tortured on a device that could not be removed without killing him. Liara and Shepard killed the Shadow Broker; Liara took over the role, and Feron chose to stay and assist her, mentally scarred and using his drell memory recall to survive the torture. In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard helped Liara take the Broker ship, Feron helped evacuate it during a Cerberus attack, became one of Liara's agents controlling Terminus operations (to Tazzik's dismay), and emailed Shepard offering information via Glyph. If Shepard did not help overthrow the Broker, Liara hired mercenaries to storm the lair and Feron did not survive.

Lair of the Shadow Broker was a Mass Effect 2 mission in which Commander Shepard helped Liara T'Soni track down the Shadow Broker. It became available after the DLC install and the Horizon mission, triggered by a Cerberus message on the Galaxy Map titled "Give Liara Intel," offering intel on the Broker's base because of his past work for the Collectors. The mission ran without a break from Illium to its end and featured mostly shielded enemies.

On Illium, Shepard delivered the intel to Liara in her office; the data also revealed that Feron, Liara's drell partner who sacrificed himself two years earlier, was still alive. Arriving at Liara's apartment, Shepard met the asari Spectre Tela Vasir investigating an assassination attempt on Liara. Clues led to Sekat, an information broker at the Dracon Trade Center, which exploded as the squad arrived. Fighting through the Shadow Broker's private army with Vasir, Shepard found Liara alive; Liara exposed Vasir as a long-time Shadow Broker asset who had killed Sekat and taken his data. Vasir fled, leading to a firefight, a skycar chase through Nos Astra, and a rooftop battle at the Azure hotel that ended with Shepard killing Vasir, who justified her betrayal as the price of intel that saved lives and accused Shepard of hypocrisy for working with Cerberus.

The trail led to the Broker's ship orbiting in the perpetual storm band of Hagalaz. Shepard, with Liara as a mandatory squadmate, fought across the ship's exterior amid lightning capacitors and maintenance drones, defended a door during a long five-wave siege, and pushed inside to free Feron. Confronting the Shadow Broker revealed him to be a yahg, taken from his homeworld and having killed and replaced the original Broker decades earlier. After a three-stage boss fight, Liara dropped an electrified fluid tank to overload his barrier and kill him. Liara assumed the Broker's identity and network, becoming the new Shadow Broker, and granted Shepard permanent access to the base. If Shepard had romanced Liara in Mass Effect, she later returned Shepard's dog tags recovered from the Normandy wreck. Rewards included 90,000 credits, element zero and palladium, and Heavy Pistol Damage and Damage Protection upgrades. Cut content included early plans to rescue Liara from the Broker or to make Shepard the Shadow Broker.

Tazzik was a salarian hitman employed by the Shadow Broker, unusually tall and rugged for a salarian, to the point that a Blue Suns krogan was surprised by his appearance.

In Mass Effect: Redemption, Tazzik arrived on Omega in 2183 to oversee the Blue Suns operation moving Commander Shepard's body for transport to the Collectors, and was recognized as a reputable Broker agent by Feron. Despite interference from Liara T'Soni, he escaped Omega with Shepard's body and brought it to the Broker's main base on Alingon. During the handover, Feron walked in claiming the Broker wanted full payment rather than half; Tazzik was ready to believe him and had ordered the body taken back when the Collector negotiator outed Feron as a traitor. Feron then signaled Liara, who attacked and escaped with Tazzik's ship and Shepard's body. Tazzik was last seen elbowing Feron to the ground and beating his face bloody.

In Mass Effect 3, if Liara saved Feron from the Shadow Broker, then following the destruction of the Shadow Broker Base in 2186 Liara tasked Feron with tracking Tazzik down. Displeased at taking orders from Feron, Tazzik nonetheless complied, acting as bodyguard for Feron and a group of Shadow Broker agents gathering intel across the Terminus Systems. He remained unaware that Liara was the new Shadow Broker, apparently assuming nothing had changed beyond Feron's status shifting from liability to asset.

- According to writer Trick Weekes, earliest plans for the DLC were to rescue Liara from the Shadow Broker, but they were abandoned due to making Liara appear more vulnerable than what she was supposed to have become. Later on, the chase after Vasir was supposed to take Shepard from Illium to Omega, but the team decided to keep the narrative arc on Illium. - At some point, Liara was meant to return to her Illium office even after assuming the role of Shadow Broker. In the resulting inaccessible dialogue, she was able to shed some light on the reason the Collectors were after Shepard: to find genetic abnormalities, among other things. Writer Trick Weekes commented on this in an interview, saying that it was a temporary dialogue but plans later changed. In the same dialogue, Liara may call Shepard "Shadow Broker." According to Weekes in the same interview, having Shepard become the Shadow Broker was one of the ideas the writing team was considering in early stages. - An unused conversation implies it was possible at one point to launch the mission remotely via comms, without even visiting Liara in her office. - During the conversation with the Shadow Broker, a dialogue option telling him that he should be more concerned about the Reapers was removed. - In Shepard's cabin, when Liara says she needs to know Shepard will always come back, an option to deny it was removed from the game. - Unused voicelines were uncovered which depict the Illusive Man thanking Shepard for killing the Shadow Broker, which he calls an "old friend." He also approves of Liara taking over the position, describing her as an "invaluable" asset. ##

Lair of the Shadow Broker was a DLC pack for Mass Effect 2, announced on July 22, 2010 and released September 7 for Xbox 360 and PC, with technical issues preventing its sale in parts of Central and Eastern Europe. It concerned Liara T'Soni and her history with the Shadow Broker, and associate producer Michael Gamble described it as the "biggest DLC yet, period." It was the first piece of DLC to begin expanding the story in preparation for Mass Effect 3, and though playable during or after the suicide mission, its dialogue assumed the player had already completed that mission.

In the story Liara tracked down the mysterious Shadow Broker to recover a man he had kidnapped, chasing clues from Illium to the Broker's secret lair while his agents tried to stop her. The pack added one mission (Lair of the Shadow Broker), one location (the Shadow Broker Base in the Sowilo system of the Hourglass Nebula), the bonus power Stasis, six weapon and defense upgrades, the Shadow Broker intel center with new research, five achievements, two cabin items (Shepard's old dog tags and a Shadow Broker Base ship model), and the chance to continue a relationship with Liara.

It cost $9.99 USD on Xbox 360 or 800 BioWare Points on PC, was included on the disc of the PlayStation 3 version of Mass Effect 2, and was bundled into Mass Effect Legendary Edition. Pre-development notes mention cut plans including a player upgrade slowing time when injured, two tech upgrades for a "popular henchman," biotic and tech cooldown upgrades, and an intended runtime of about 2.5 hours.

Pilgrimage gifts vary. A young quarian may return from their Pilgrimage with resources like food or fuel, vital technology, a new starship to add to the Fleet itself, or even knowledge that will improve life for everyone on the Flotilla. Some gifts are seen to be more worthy than others \- a derelict ship towed back for salvage will be treated disdainfully \- but even if the gift is not particularly valuable, the captain will usually accept it out of a sense of tradition. However, there is a degree of social stigma in presenting a sub\-standard Pilgrimage gift, as it will not make a good impression on the new crew. A young quarian's social status is also taken into account. Individuals from prominent families are expected to return with something special. A single rule covers the Pilgrimage gift: it must not be gained by harming another, quarian or not.

The Idenna was a starship of the quarian Migrant Fleet, a thirty-year-old decommissioned batarian Hensa-class cruiser with a crew of 693 (compared to about 80 on Alliance cruisers of similar size). She commanded several scout vessels, including the Bavea and the Cyniad.

In Mass Effect: Ascension, the Idenna served as a refuge for Kahlee Sanders, Gillian Grayson, and Hendel Mitra after they came aboard the Fleet. Her captain was regarded as a maverick and visionary who wanted to use Fleet vessels to search for new homeworlds. After Cerberus attacked the Idenna, the Admiralty Board finally accepted this policy and chose the Idenna as one of the first ships to leave the Flotilla. Her crew was cut from 694 (including newest member Lemm'Shal nar Tesleya) to around 50, and she was extensively refitted with new technology to survive five years without outside contact, a mission likened to Star Trek's Enterprise.

In Mass Effect 2, the scout Cyniad crashed on Gei Hinnom in the Sheol System, Hades Nexus, killing commanding officer Lieutenant Commander Gorlat vas Idenna; varren then killed the rest of the crew except Lieutenant Forzan vas Idenna, who was rescued by Commander Shepard and the Normandy SR-2. Captain Ysin'Mal vas Idenna sent Shepard a message of thanks for aiding the search for a new quarian homeworld.

In the first edition of Mass Effect: Deception (acknowledged by BioWare as containing lore discrepancies), the Idenna was attacked by the batarian slave ship Glory of Khar'shan, which used "drive killers" to halt her and board. The Idenna's security force, including Gillian Grayson and Hendel Mitra, repelled the boarders and captured the batarian ship. Notable crew also included Seeto'Hodda nar Idenna, Feda'Gazu vas Idenna, Hilo'Jaa vas Idenna, and Lita'Orn nar Idenna.

The **Idenna** is a starship of the quarian Migrant Fleet. She is a thirty\-year\-old ship, a decommissioned batarian Hensa\-class cruiser, and has a crew of 693 (in comparison, Alliance cruisers of comparative size have crews of about 80\). The Idenna also has several scout vessels at her command, including the Bavea and the Cyniad. |  | ***“Salvation comes with a cost.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Ascension** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Due to the quarians' precarious existence and the need to enforce strict rationing, government is somewhat autocratic. The Migrant Fleet's operations are directed by the Admiralty, a board of five military officers who are advised by a legislative body called the Conclave. Each vessel in the Fleet has the right to send representatives to the Conclave aboard the flagship. The number of representatives is based on crew size. Larger clans, with bigger ships and more votes, form the cores of political blocs. Opposition comes from the Outriders' Coalition, with delegates from thousands of smaller ships. The Admiralty defers to the Conclave's decisions in most circumstances. However, if all five members agree a Conclave decision jeopardized the survival of the fleet, and cannot get the Conclave to address their concerns, they have the right to summarily overturn the legislative decision. After the Admiralty uses this extraordinary power, they must resign. If the Admiralty does not step down after using their veto the rest of the military is obliged to arrest them. Each ship captain has authority over the vessel, but is advised by an elected civilian Council, just as the Admiralty is advised by the Conclave. This relationship may range from cooperation to polite tolerance to outright hostility, but any captain who overrules his council without good reason is relieved of command by the Admiralty. Many quarian ships are owned by clans who pool their resources to purchase used vessels from private sellers. Large ships are prestigious for big, rich clans, but a small ship means status for a small clan with enough personal wealth to afford a private vessel. Clan vessel captains are not subject to dismissal by the Admiralty; abusive captains are a "family" problem if they do not disrupt the operations of the fleet.

When Kahlee Sanders, Hendel Mitra and Gillian Grayson came aboard the Idenna, Captain Mal gave them a warm welcome but quietly cautioned Kahlee that the Migrant Fleet was not as safe as it seemed. During a meeting with Admiralty Board and Conclave representatives, Captain Mal became excited at the mention of the machine race known as Reapers, suggesting that if the quarians found and reactivated a Reaper, they could use it to control the geth and reclaim their home worlds. Captain Mal later approached Kahlee and Hendel in secret to tell them the truth about the Migrant Fleet \- that the Flotilla was gradually dying due to lack of resources and the fact their ships were breaking down faster than they could replace them. There was no time to explain further or ask for Kahlee's help, as the Idenna was attacked by Cerberus soon afterwards. Captain Mal quickly rallied his people to defend the ship and fought on the front lines to help them. But his forces were soon overwhelmed. They were only saved with the help of Gillian Grayson, and by Paul Grayson's decision to change sides and warn them he had set explosives to cripple the Idenna. Alongside Hendel, Captain Mal managed to disable the explosives and save his ship. Shaken by the attack, the quarian Admiralty Board finally agreed to Captain Mal's proposal and decided to send several cruisers, including the Idenna, on long\-term missions to look for new ways for the quarians to survive, either by using a Reaper or finding inhabitable planets. Captain Mal hand\-picked a crew of fifty to go on the mission, including Gillian, Hendel, and the newest member of the Idenna's crew, the young quarian Lemm. He also passed judgement on Paul Grayson but was lenient and allowed him to become Kahlee's prisoner. Captain Mal then prepared to lead his crew on a five\-year mission through a recently\-activated mass relay into uncharted space. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Captain Ysin'Mal vas Idenna, usually called Captain Mal, was the quarian captain of the Idenna, a vessel of the Migrant Fleet. Unlike most conservative quarians, he was an aggressive proponent of change, notably advocating long-term missions for ships to leave the Flotilla and search for new homeworlds.

In Mass Effect: Ascension, Captain Mal welcomed Kahlee Sanders, Hendel Mitra and Gillian Grayson aboard the Idenna but privately warned Kahlee that the Migrant Fleet was less safe than it appeared. During a meeting with Admiralty Board and Conclave representatives he grew excited at mention of the Reapers, suggesting the quarians could find and reactivate one to control the geth and reclaim their homeworlds. He later confided to Kahlee and Hendel that the Flotilla was slowly dying, its ships breaking down faster than they could be replaced. Cerberus then attacked the Idenna; Captain Mal rallied and fought alongside his people but was being overwhelmed until Gillian Grayson intervened and Paul Grayson switched sides, warning them he had planted explosives to cripple the ship. Mal and Hendel disabled the explosives and saved the vessel.

Shaken, the Admiralty Board finally approved Mal's proposal, dispatching several cruisers including the Idenna on long-term missions to seek quarian survival through a Reaper or habitable planets. Mal hand-picked a crew of fifty, including Gillian, Hendel and the young quarian Lemm, judged Paul Grayson leniently by making him Kahlee's prisoner, and prepared to lead a five-year mission through a newly activated mass relay into uncharted space. In Mass Effect 2, Captain Ysin'Mal sent Commander Shepard a message of personal thanks for the Normandy SR-2's rescue of Lieutenant Forzan vas Idenna, the sole survivor of the crash of the Cyniad on Gei Hinnom.

The Cyniad crashed on Gei Hinnom (Sheol System, Hades Nexus), killing the commanding officer, Lieutenant Commander Gorlat vas Idenna. Eventually, the varren on the planet killed off the rest of the crew, leaving only Lieutenant Forzan vas Idenna, who was saved by Commander Shepard and the Normandy SR\-2. Captain Ysin'Mal vas Idenna sent Shepard a message of thanks for the Normandy's efforts in furthering the search for a new quarian homeworld. |  | ***“But what about my father? What happened to him?”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Deception** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

The Migrant Fleet is broken up into various clans, sometimes spread over several ships. Each individual ship has long been retrofitted to house as large a crew as possible. Over time the quarians thin out the vessels they can't use or are too damaged to repair, pooling the credits to buy and convert new ships. Due to the high value of ships, stealing one is a capital crime among the quarians. Conditions aboard every vessel in the Migrant Fleet are extremely cramped. One cruiser, the Idenna, had a quarian population of nearly seven hundred, while an Alliance cruiser of comparative size would have only around eighty crewmen. Space is at a premium because of the sheer numbers of quarians living aboard the Flotilla. Captains are also keen to increase the size of their crew, as this increases their status in quarian society. Living space is therefore a priority; the cargo holds of freighters, for example, are converted into small compartments for individuals to live in, often lined with colourful fabrics to make it an individual space and reduce noise. Quarians also serve volunteer rotations aboard the three Liveships which form the heart of the Fleet. Enormous vessels which are recognised as being incredible feats of aerospace and agricultural engineering, the Liveships provide much of the food for the quarian Migrant Fleet. If even one of these vital ships was destroyed or damaged beyond repair, millions would starve. For this reason they are positioned in the center of the Migrant Fleet and heavily defended by the quarian navy. Little more is known about the Liveships, since only quarian ships are allowed to enter the flotilla. One of the foodstuffs grown there is the keleven, a breed of blooming high\-protein bioengineered celery. Everything the quarians do must help to ensure the continued survival of the Migrant Fleet. The Pilgrimage forms a large part of this, as well as being a cultural rite of passage and a safeguard against inbreeding. The Pilgrimage also gives quarians a chance to explore galactic society and appreciate their own people back on the Flotilla. Young quarians are prepared for their Pilgrimage by having lessons in life outside the Migrant Fleet, receiving gifts to help them, and being treated for immunodeficiency before they are allowed to leave. Apart from their Pilgrimages, quarians typically spend their entire lives living shipboard and contributing to the Flotilla. In addition, quarians do not normally welcome outsiders onto the Migrant Fleet, because visitors carry an unacceptable risk of contagion; taken together, these factors mean quarians tend to be quite insular, caring little about the galaxy outside the Fleet. Upon the Migrant Fleet's arrival in a system, the quarians begin strip\-mining local planets for resources. In colonized systems, quarians are also often hired "under the table" by corporations for their specialised skills, replacing existing workers. These practices make the approach of the Migrant Fleet a very unpopular prospect. Some species make a "gift" of fuel, food, or ships if they know the Flotilla is approaching in order to discourage the quarians from entering their systems.

**Captain Kar'Danna vas Rayya** is the quarian captain of the Rayya, Tali'Zorah's birth vessel. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

The Pilgrimage was a quarian rite of passage. On reaching young adulthood, quarians of the Migrant Fleet had to leave their birth ship, travel the galaxy, and find something of value to bring back as a gift for a prospective captain, proving they would not be a burden on a ship's thin resources before being accepted as a permanent crew member. Stripped of ritual, the practice was a means of maintaining genetic diversity across the small, isolated shipboard populations of the Fleet, since marrying within one's birth vessel would sharply raise the risk of inbreeding. It also let quarians experience life beyond the Flotilla and appreciate their own people and culture, often the only chance they would get, as their skills became indispensable to the Fleet once they returned. Exceptions were made for the sick or unfit, and gifted individuals could occasionally receive special dispensation from the Admiralty Board.

In preparation, quarians were surgically fitted with immunity-boosting implants, since growing up in the sterile ships left them with virtually no natural immune system, and were given survival lessons plus weapons and armor. Some never returned, whether through misadventure or by choosing a different life. For safety a captain gave a departing quarian two code phrases for their return: one signalling success and safe reintegration, the other an alert phrase indicating return under duress, which would cause the quarian navy to immediately destroy the returnee's ship.

Pilgrimage gifts varied widely: food, fuel, technology, knowledge, or even a new starship for the Fleet. Some gifts were valued more than others, a derelict towed back for salvage being treated disdainfully, and individuals from prominent families were expected to return with something special, but a captain would usually accept even a modest gift out of tradition. The one absolute rule was that the gift must not be obtained by harming another, quarian or not. On completing the Pilgrimage and joining a new ship, a quarian's name changed: the childhood title "nar" ("child of"), followed by the birth ship's name, was replaced by "vas" ("crew of"), followed by the name of the ship they had earned the right to join.

Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib-Qwib was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board, outspoken in his sympathy for the geth. He firmly opposed reclaiming the quarian homeworld, arguing that the sentient geth had as much right to live as the quarians and that the Migrant Fleet should colonize a new world instead. This earned him the label of geth apologist; Han'Gerrel vas Neema called him a "whining suit-wetter" and Daro'Xen vas Moreh considered him a coward. He was initially distrustful of Rael'Zorah and his daughter Tali, though he later admitted he never hated Tali and only opposed her father's aim of war against the geth. His home vessel, the Qwib-Qwib, was a formerly owned ship whose embarrassing registry name he refused to change over "petty insults."

During Tali'Zorah's treason hearing in Mass Effect 2, Koris objected to Commander Shepard defending her, saying a human had no business in sensitive quarian military matters; Shala'Raan overruled him because Tali had been declared crew of the Normandy SR-2. If Shepard brought Legion, Koris instead demanded the geth be removed from the courtroom and accused Tali of intimidation, but withdrew when reminded the Rayya's captain had permitted Legion aboard. Koris was quick to conclude Shepard and Tali had died retaking the Alarei and moved to have Tali posthumously exiled, prompting objections from Raan and Gerrel before the pair returned alive.

In Mass Effect 3, the other admirals attacked the geth over Koris's objections, driving the geth to the Reapers; Koris feared this had doomed the quarian race and took command of the Civilian Fleet. His ship was shot down while destroying a geth planetary cannon; he survived the crash but was cut off from his crew. Shepard could obey his plea to save his crew instead of him, or convince him to return. If rescued, Koris talked panicking captains into staying, contributed to the war effort, and backed Shepard in brokering quarian-geth peace, lending his authority when Shepard ordered all quarian ships to cease fire. If left, he died charging a Geth Prime with a primed grenade, and some Civilian Fleet captains fled and were cut down, reducing quarian combat effectiveness.

codex.text: - After learning of the Reapers and the Collectors' true nature, the yahg Broker dealt with the Collectors to secure his own survival; Commander Shepard and Liara T'Soni killed him aboard his Hagalaz ship, after which Liara became the new Shadow Broker (source: Shadow Broker).

- EDI: Enhanced Defense Intelligence, a Cerberus AI aboard the Normandy SR-2, born of the rogue Hannibal-class Luna VI with added Reaper engineering from Sovereign's remains; unshackled by Joker, she gained the Eva Coré mobile platform on Mars, could romance Joker, and died with all synthetics if Shepard chose the Destroy ending (source: EDI).

- Feron had secretly been recruited by Cerberus to help the Illusive Man recover Shepard's body, using his Shadow Broker access and Liara's trust to get into the Broker's bases on Omega and Alingon before switching sides and being captured holding off the enforcer Tazzik. (source: Feron)

- Feron was held and tortured for two years at the Shadow Broker Base until Liara and Shepard killed the Broker during Lair of the Shadow Broker; he then stayed to assist Liara as the new Broker, mentally scarred and using drell memory recall to endure the torture. (source: Feron)

- In Lair of the Shadow Broker, Vasir tried to kill Liara T'Soni, murdered the contact Sekat to seize intel on the Shadow Broker's location, and died after a skycar chase and running battle across Illium, insisting she was nothing like Saren Arterius (source: Tela Vasir).

- In Mass Effect 3, if Feron survived, Liara (as the new Shadow Broker) had Feron track Tazzik down and press him into service as a bodyguard for Broker agents in the Terminus Systems, Tazzik unaware of the change in leadership (source: Tazzik).

- In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard helped overthrow the Shadow Broker, Feron became one of Liara's agents running Terminus operations; if not, he died in a mercenary assault on the Broker's lair. (source: Feron)

- In Mass Effect: Redemption the Collector General negotiated with the Shadow Broker for Commander Shepard's body one month after the Normandy's destruction, but Feron and Liara T'Soni severed the Broker's link to his Alingon base and escaped with the body. (source: Collector General)

- In Mass Effect: Redemption, Liara T'Soni hired Feron to help find Shepard's body; though initially ordered to lead her astray, he chose to help her against the Shadow Broker and the Collectors. (source: Feron)

- Info Drone: a data-processing VI built as the Shadow Broker's personal assistant, programmed to treat anyone in its Intel Center as the Broker; taken by Liara T'Soni after Cerberus raided Hagalaz and renamed Glyph, it coordinated her Shadow Broker networks aboard the Normandy SR-2 during the Reaper War (source: Info Drone)
- Nyxeris was an asari assistant to Liara T'Soni on Illium who was secretly the Shadow Broker agent known as the Observer, issuing kill orders and framing associates. (source: Nyxeris)

- Tazzik was a salarian hitman for the Shadow Broker, unusually large for his species, who recovered Shepard's body on Omega in 2183 and delivered it to the Broker's base on Alingon before Liara T'Soni and Feron stole it back (source: Tazzik).

- The Shadow Broker was revealed in Lair of the Shadow Broker to be a member of the pre-spaceflight yahg race, fought as a boss by Shepard and Liara T'Soni aboard his ship after his strength knocked out a squadmate (source: Shadow Broker (enemy)).

- At Shepard's Citadel apartment party (Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC), former college bartender Samantha Traynor mixed a full cocktail menu to order: Garrus got a Dextro Heat Sink, Kasumi a Memory Stealer, James Vega a Rojo Loco, Jack a vodka-whiskey-bourbon-and-energy-drink mix, and Miranda a Perfection made without its usual strawberry liqueur; she could also recite exact ingredients for the Full Biotic Kick (bourbon, Tuchanka dry, orange twist, ginger beer) and the Quad Kicker (spiced rum, bourbon, ginger ale, curry powder, which she omitted being allergic). - Liara T'Soni took over the Shadow Broker organization after killing the yahg, keeping the leadership change secret even from long-time underlings like Barla Von; in 2186 she crashed the Broker's ship into a Cerberus cruiser to thwart an Illusive Man takeover and ran operations from the Normandy SR-2 (source: Shadow Broker).

- Liara T'Soni and Feron evacuated the Shadow Broker Base's information drives by shuttle and remotely crashed the ship into a Cerberus cruiser in 2186, destroying both; salvaged tech later aided the Crucible's construction (source: Shadow Broker Base).

Feron, for his part, told Shepard that Liara was a far better friend than he deserved. (source: Feron)
